title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past Gameplay Shows Letten and Geralt’s New Chain
description: New Songs of the Past gameplay takes Geralt through Letten, shows an early quest, and demonstrates the Witcher 3 expansion’s new silver chain combat.
body: CD Projekt Red has released a longer public gameplay look at The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past, giving players a clearer sense of how Geralt’s return to the Path will actually play. The footage moves through Letten, an entirely new open-world region, and shows exploration, questing, combat and one of the expansion’s most noticeable mechanical additions: Geralt’s silver chain.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Geralt rides Roach toward a large timber-built settlement in Letten, surrounded by stone walls, trees and wildflowers.

contentBlocks.text:
Songs of the Past takes Geralt to **Letten**, a new open-world region that CD Projekt Red describes as idyllic on the surface but hiding something sinister underneath. The longer gameplay showcase makes that contrast much easier to see. Geralt travels through pastoral countryside and lived-in settlements before the journey turns toward darker woodland and thorn-covered spaces.

Letten is presented as a region with its own identity rather than an extension of Velen or Toussaint. Reporting from the gameplay showcase says the area draws on rural Polish and English influences, with local customs, architecture and a landscape relatively untouched by war. The result is a setting that looks peaceful enough to invite exploration while still fitting The Witcher 3’s habit of placing unsettling stories behind picturesque scenery.

CD Projekt Red has confirmed that Letten brings new quests, characters, locations and secrets, with Songs of the Past scheduled for 2027.
contentBlocks.heading: The new footage gives us a proper look at Letten

contentBlocks.text:
The gameplay follows part of an early quest called **A Bed of Thorns**, giving us a better sense of how the expansion moves between exploration, conversation, investigation and combat.

Rather than functioning as a detached combat demonstration, the sequence is built around Geralt following a trail through Letten and gradually moving toward a more threatening environment. That familiar rhythm matters because it suggests Songs of the Past is extending The Witcher 3’s established quest design instead of treating the expansion as a separate action showcase.

The expansion is also tied closely to Dandelion and his homeland. CD Projekt Red has positioned Letten as a place connected to the bard’s past, giving the new region a personal narrative reason to exist rather than simply adding another map for Geralt to explore.
contentBlocks.heading: An early quest shows how Songs of the Past is structured

contentBlocks.text:
The most obvious mechanical addition shown in the new footage is Geralt’s **silver chain**. The showcase demonstrates it as another way to control space during combat, letting Geralt interfere with enemies and create openings before following up with his familiar swords and Signs.

The chain does not appear to replace The Witcher 3’s existing combat system. Instead, it expands Geralt’s toolkit while keeping the core loop recognizable: positioning, sword attacks, Signs and preparation still sit at the center of encounters.

That makes the addition more interesting than a purely cosmetic callback. It gives returning players something new to experiment with while preserving the combat language of the original game.
contentBlocks.heading: Geralt’s silver chain adds a new combat option

contentBlocks.text:
The gameplay remains immediately recognizable as The Witcher 3. Geralt explores an open environment, speaks with characters, investigates clues and gets pulled into combat when the trail turns dangerous.

At the same time, Songs of the Past is arriving alongside the remastered version of The Witcher 3, and the presentation reflects a broader effort to modernize the game’s feel and presentation for current hardware. That context is important: the expansion is not being built as though the 2015 version of The Witcher 3 has remained untouched for more than a decade.

For returning players, that combination may be one of the expansion’s biggest strengths. Songs of the Past can preserve the structure and tone people remember while benefiting from work designed to make The Witcher 3 feel less dated in 2026 and beyond.
contentBlocks.heading: Songs of the Past still feels like The Witcher 3 — just more modern

contentBlocks.text:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past is scheduled for **2027** on **PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch 2**. CD Projekt Red and Fool’s Theory are developing the expansion together.

Our [original Songs of the Past reveal](/stories/witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-gamescom-2026-reveal/) established Letten and Geralt’s reason for returning. This longer gameplay showcase is more useful because it shows what that return actually looks like: a new region built around exploration and investigation, familiar Witcher quest structure, new monsters and a combat tool that meaningfully expands Geralt’s options.

CD Projekt Red has not announced a more specific release date. Until then, Songs of the Past already looks less like a nostalgic epilogue and more like a substantial new chapter built on the systems that made The Witcher 3 work in the first place.
contentBlocks.heading: Geralt returns to the Path in 2027
